newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore-Chile bank deal a helpful step -executive.
newsitem.headline: Singapore-Chile bank deal a helpful step -executive.

text.p: The president of Chile's banking trade asssociation said on Wednesday a memorandum of understanding signed with bankers in Singapore would help his country achieve its goal of being a financial services capital.

"We want to become a platform for financial business in Latin America and from that point of view I think information coming from this part of the world will be quite relevant," Hernan Somerville told Reuters.
Somerville, president of the Chilean Association of Banks and Financial Institutions, was in Singapore to sign the agreement with Ng Kee Choe, chairman of the Association of Banks in Singapore.

The agreement will see an exchange of information, skills and experience between the two bodies in an effort to build closer relations with the financial sectors of two nations that see themselves as gateways to wider hinterlands.

Somerville said Chile was rapidly moving from being a commodities and manufacturing-based economy to a financial and services-based economy and had much to learn from the experience of Singapore which had undergone a similar transition.
"Chile will become more and more a service economy, so from that point of view the experience of this part of the world, especially in Singapore is very important to us," he said.
